questions.question_text: Solve $\cos 36^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{11}$, giving $x$ correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Used $\sin 36^{\circ}$ instead of $\cos 36^{\circ}$ in the multiplication.
Divided $11$ by $\cos 36^{\circ}$ instead of multiplying, as if $x$ were in the denominator.
Evaluated $\cos 36^{\circ}$ but forgot to multiply by the $11$.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (B) at (3.400,0);\coordinate (C) at (3.400,2.656);\draw (A)--(B) node[midway,below] {$10\text{ m}$};\draw (B)--(C) node[midway,right] {$x$};\draw (C)--(A);\coordinate (va) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(A)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(B)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$38^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.6cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=B--A--C};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which trigonometric ratio should be used to find $x$?

options.why: Treated the $10$ m side as the hypotenuse, but it lies alongside the $38^{\circ}$ angle.
Treated $x$ as the hypotenuse, but $x$ is opposite the $38^{\circ}$ angle.

questions.solution_text:
The $10$ m side is adjacent to the $38^{\circ}$ angle $(A)$.
$x$ is opposite the $38^{\circ}$ angle $(O)$.
The ratio using $O$ and $A$ is $\tan$.

[/tikz]
A $7.2$ m ladder leans against a vertical wall at $65^{\circ}$ to the level ground.
How far up the wall does the ladder reach, correct to $1$ decimal place?

options.why: Used $\cos 65^{\circ}$, which gives the distance from the wall to the foot of the ladder.
Used $\tan 65^{\circ}$, treating the ladder as the side adjacent to the angle.
Divided $7.2$ by $\sin 65^{\circ}$; this makes the height longer than the ladder, which is impossible.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (B) at (0,0);\coordinate (A) at (0,2.983);\coordinate (C) at (3.200,0);\draw (A)--(B);\draw (B)--(C) node[midway,below] {$x$};\draw (C)--(A) node[midway,above right] {$12.5\text{ m}$};\coordinate (va) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(A)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(B)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$47^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.7cm,angle eccentricity=1.6] {angle=B--A--C};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
The marked angle is at the top of the triangle.
Find $x$ correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Used $\cos 47^{\circ}$, but from the top angle the vertical side is the adjacent one, not $x$.
Used $\tan 47^{\circ}$, treating the $12.5$ m side as adjacent instead of the hypotenuse.
Divided $12.5$ by $\sin 47^{\circ}$; this makes $x$ longer than the hypotenuse, which is impossible.

questions.solution_text:
From the $47^{\circ}$ angle, $x$ is the opposite side and $12.5$ m is the hypotenuse.
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{O}{H}$
$\sin 47^{\circ}=\dfrac{x}{12.5}$
$12.5\sin 47^{\circ}=x$
$x\approx 9.1\text{ m}$
